title: YEEZY BOOST 350 V2
description: The first adidas Yeezy 350 V2 release of 2019 gets colored up in a pale blue/green hue for a clean, neutral upper incorporating a semi-translucent vent at the lateral side that matches up with the translucent outsole. This ‘Hyperspace’ edition features a flexible Primeknit upper and full-length Boost cushioning—both iconic features of the Yeezy 350 V2 sneaker. This shoe released March 2019 exclusively in select cities in Africa, the Middle East, India and Asia Pacific.

title: YEEZY BOOST 700 V2
description: The Yeezy Boost 700 V2 ‘Static’ is an update to the original Wave Runner. The upper features a slightly reworked design, while the midsole stays the same. This new edition showcases an understated colorway made up of soft, neutral shades. The layered composition of the upper, featuring a mesh base with welded reflective overlays and leather paneling, is finished in varying shades of grey and white. The silhouette’s signature bulky midsole, finished in matching white, is supported underfoot by a black rubber outsole.

title: YEEZY BOOST 350 V2
description: The Yeezy Boost 350 V2 'Yeshaya Reflective' enhances the visual impact of the neutral two-tone Primeknit upper with reflective fibers woven into the build. Additional reflective hits appear on the rope laces and signature three-stripes that run down the interior of the rear collar, ultimately allowing the sneaker to shine in low-light conditions. A subtle yellow finish is applied to the semi-translucent rubber midsole, fitted with a Boost unit for lightweight cushioning.

description:
Background: Designed by Demna and his team, the Men's Sleeveless Second Skin was originally designed and intended to be given to the Homeless to be a base layer, and they would add or keep only the Second Skin on depending on the weather. 

Though a look for it was taken for the initial Lookbook of YGEBB, it was not edited and released; the look was modeled by Bilal Cudjoe.

It was initially sold on yeezygap.com in Black and Dark Green, modeled by John Andrew Adams.

The retail version did not feature any major changes from the lookbook/sample version. The initial prototype by Balenciaga did have a YZY Logo instead of a GAP Logo.
